headline: Highest-leverage upgrades by evidence: a vol/trend regime filter gating net exposure (strong evidence, directly targets the 2.22 down-capture) plus vol-scaled sizing; drop always-on index puts (strong evidence they are pure drag); freeze any config for at least 21-33 trades (~2.5-3.3 weeks at current trade rate) before a verdict because weekly changes mathematically prevent statistical significance; a 60-to-15-min cadence bump costs only ~$46-83/mo at Opus 4.8 pricing but requires switching cache TTL to 1h.
evidence: (1) Intraday momentum — STRONG for indices, MODERATE for single names: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou 'Market Intraday Momentum' (JFE 2018, SPY 1993-2013) shows first half-hour return predicts last half-hour return, R2=1.6%, stronger on volatile/high-volume days, replicated on 10+ ETFs — implication: avoid open-print entries (the Jul 27 $300k QQQ open sweep loss is exactly the documented noise), prefer entries after 10:30 ET with a last-hour momentum confirmation for index hedges. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X18301351 ; https://alphaarchitect.com/attention-prop-traders-the-first-half-hour-of-trading-predicts-the-last-half-hour/

(2) Meta-labeling — MODERATE evidence for the technique, WEAK feasibility at ~100 trades: Lopez de Prado AFML + Hudson & Thames replication show secondary gates raise precision/F1, but published successes train on thousands of labels; with ~100 trades only a 2-3 feature logistic regression or deterministic rule-filter (e.g. block entries when loss-streak>=2 AND ATR-percentile>80) is fittable without severe overfit — a full ML secondary model at N=100 is statistically indefensible. https://hudsonthames.org/does-meta-labeling-add-to-signal-efficacy-triple-barrier-method/ ; https://www.quantconnect.com/forum/discussion/14706/why-meta-labeling-is-not-a-silver-bullet/

(3) Vol targeting — STRONG for momentum-tilted books (this system qualifies): Moreira-Muir (JF 2017) find vol-managed portfolios add ~0.15 Sharpe and win in ~80% of cases; Cederburg et al. (JFE 2020) temper it — only 8/103 portfolios significantly improve, concentrated in momentum strategies. Vol-scaled sizing (target risk / realized vol) beats fixed Kelly fraction specifically on down-capture because it mechanically de-levers into vol spikes. https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w22208/w22208.pdf ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X2030132X

(4) Regime filters — STRONG, best fit for the 2.22 down-capture: Faber's 10-month/200-day MA filter (2007) cut max drawdown to 9.5% in-sample and 11.7% out-of-sample while keeping equity-like CAGR; mechanism is exactly down-capture reduction (exposure goes to cash below trend). Gating NEW long entries and max gross exposure on SPY>200dma + VIX/realized-vol percentile is the single most evidence-backed change for red-day losses. https://www.trendfollowing.com/whitepaper/CMT-Simple.pdf ; https://quantpedia.com/strategies/asset-class-trend-following

(5) Protective sleeve — STRONG evidence AGAINST always-on index puts: CBOE PPUT delivered ~2.5% annualized excess return over 32 years, identical to a 36.5% equity/63.5% cash mix (the put premium is pure drag); AQR 'Risk and Return of Equity Index Collar Strategies' shows collars (CLL: 5.2% vs 7.3% unhedged, 71% of return at 67% of vol) beat bought puts but still lag simple de-grossing; beta-hedge shorts are cheapest but carry basis risk on a small-cap book vs SPY. Ranking for this system: regime-gated de-grossing > collar on core > beta short > standing OTM puts. https://www.aqr.com/-/media/AQR/Documents/Journal-Articles/Risk-and-Return.pdf ; https://www.cboe.com/insights/posts/benchmark-indices-series-hedging-downside-exposure-with-pput-cll-and-cllz-indices

(6) Walk-forward math (computed for win 40%, 3.3:1): expectancy=0.72R, per-trade SD=2.11R, per-trade Sharpe=0.34. Trades needed to reject zero expectancy: ~24 at 95% one-sided (skew-adjusted Lopez de Prado MinTRL: 21), 33 at 95% two-sided, 46 at 99%. At ~10 round trips/week that is 2.4-3.3 weeks frozen minimum per verdict; win-rate itself is +/-21.5pp at N=20, +/-9.6pp at N=100. Framework: Bailey & Lopez de Prado PSR/MinTRL and Deflated Sharpe (each config change is another 'trial' that should further deflate significance). https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1821643 ; https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2460551

(7) LLM-trading literature — MODERATE for memory/reflection, WEAK for debate/multi-agent: FinMem ablations show layered memory + risk-character settings drive its gains (arxiv 2311.13743); FinAgent (KDD'24) ablations attribute gains to reflection modules and auxiliary agents (44%->54% return in one ablation); TradingAgents' debate structure has no clean ablation isolating debate benefit. Counterweight: a 2026 KDD out-of-sample study finds most LLM agents fail to beat buy-and-hold on post-cutoff data (Mar-Jul 2025), and look-ahead bias is pervasive (GPT-4o recalls S&P 500 closes <1% error inside its training window; <28% of the 250 LLM-finance papers discuss any bias). Adopt: deepen the existing lessons/postmortem memory into retrieval-at-decision-time. Skip: multi-agent debate. https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.13743 ; https://personal.ntu.edu.sg/boan/papers/KDD24_FinAgent.pdf ; https://arxiv.org/html/2412.20138v1 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.13770

(8) Cadence economics (Opus 4.8, from authoritative pricing: $5/$25 per MTok; cache read 0.1x=$0.50/M; write 1.25x=$6.25/M at 5-min TTL, 2x=$10/M at 1h TTL; min cacheable prefix 4096 tokens; 4 breakpoints max): observed decision call = ~18.0K uncached in + 7.3K cache-read + ~2.3K out = $0.151/call. 60min cadence ~$22/mo; 30min ~$41/mo; 15min ~$83/mo (21 trading days). Moving ~15K of the uncached 18K input into the cached prefix cuts per-call cost 45% to $0.084 -> 15-min cadence for ~$46/mo. Critical mechanic: at 15/30-min cadence the default 5-min TTL expires between ticks, so every call pays the write premium unless cache_control uses ttl:'1h'. Source: bundled claude-api skill pricing tables + /Users/spusapati/Personal/Investment_stratergy/state/api_usage.jsonl
surprises: The system's current tail-protection design (standing index puts, added PR #46) has the strongest evidence AGAINST it of anything researched: PPUT's 32-year record equals a 36.5/63.5 equity-cash mix — bought puts are pure drag; regime-gated de-grossing achieves the down-capture cut without the premium bleed.

Weekly strategy changes make statistical evaluation impossible by construction: at 40% win / 3.3:1 the system needs 21-33 trades (~2.5-3.3 weeks) frozen per verdict, and every mid-window PR resets the clock AND adds a multiple-testing trial that deflates significance further — the Aug 3-14 observation window at ~20 trades yields a win-rate CI of +/-21.5pp, too wide for any verdict.

Published LLM-trading performance (FinMem, FinAgent, TradingAgents) is largely inside-training-window and look-ahead-contaminated; the only 2026 out-of-sample test found most LLM agents fail to beat buy-and-hold — treat those papers as component-design guidance (memory/reflection), not as evidence the approach earns alpha.

Vol targeting is NOT a universal fix — significant in only 8/103 portfolios (Cederburg 2020) — but those 8 are momentum-type strategies, which is precisely this system's profile, so it lands in the favorable subset.

Cache ledger anomaly worth auditing: api_usage.jsonl shows a constant cache_read=7,297 with cache_write=0 on calls 52-60 minutes apart, which should be impossible under the default 5-min TTL (each call should pay a write) — either a 1h TTL is silently in effect, something else re-warms the prefix, or the ledger's cache accounting is wrong; also ~18K tokens/call of input is currently NOT cached, a 45% per-call saving left on the table.

Intraday-momentum evidence runs opposite to the current hourly clock: the documented signal is index-level first-half-hour -> last-half-hour (R2 1.6%), meaning the open is noise to avoid (the Jul 27 QQQ open-print loss was this) and the last 30 minutes is the only intraday window with a documented directional edge — a cadence increase is more valuable for exit management near the close than for more entries.
